newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products boosted by regional demand.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products boosted by regional demand.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were helped by regional demand on Wednesday, traders said.

Gasoline was slightly firmer in line with stronger NYMEX prices. Traders said supply was tighter with refinery turnarounds eating into production. Small pockets of demand were seen out of Turkey, Tunisia and Romania.
Some local refiners were considering postponing or downscaling maintenance to profit from current high margins.
Traders said the naptha market was fairly quiet with high paraffinic quality judged difficult to find, though small parcels of lower paraffinic content material were available.

Gas oil remained strong and well bid, supported by both local buying and arbitrage exports assembled in response to some $300 million of buying of 0.5 percent diesel in recent days by Singapore's Hin Leong and sister company Sanko.
A European major with a corresponding May paper position sold a cargo of 0.5 percent sulphur diesel to Singapore at $26.70 a barrel for May 5-9 lifting, up 30 cents from Tuesday.

In regional trade, 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil moved at around a $4 premium to high fob Med quotes basis Italy, while 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil changed hands at close to a $3 premium to high fob Med.
The high sulphur fuel market was well talked by traders anxious to help the pricing of cargoes into Romania, though physical cargoes were not as scarce as was said.
High sulphur was definetly overvalued at the bid numbers bandied around on Tuesday, traders said, and some added that prices may even have drifted down a $1 to $82/$83.

Tuesday's most prominent bidder became a sell enquirer, asking after Spanish bunker requirements, which were heard not urgent. The buyer was believed heartened by the aggressive numbers bid for the Portugese EdP tender.
